title: Bodhi Tree: Sacred Fig Trees You Can Visit
meta_description: These trees have planting dates because their lineage is the point: cuttings carried from Bodh Gaya. Five bodhi trees mapped in Bangkok and Singapore.
intro: Most of these trees have a planting date, because with a bodhi the lineage is the point. Cuttings are carried from tree to tree back toward Bodh Gaya, and Thai temples record the year one arrived the way they record a relic. Wat Saket's went in in 1818, brought home by two monks sent abroad by King Rama II who came back after three years with cuttings instead of the relics they were sent for. Wat Phra Kaew's dates from 1864 and grows inside the most photographed temple complex in Thailand, where almost nobody photographs it. Wat Benchamabophit's was planted in 1900, nine years after Thailand received its first direct cutting from Bodh Gaya itself. The fourth in Bangkok is Lan Pho on the lawn at Thammasat University, where the protest that brought down a dictatorship began in October 1973. Singapore's stands on Pearl's Hill.
